sections.h2: What is Polk County, Georgia like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Polk County is the most populous of the four Georgia counties in this Census comparison, with 45,514 residents estimated for July 2025. The tax commissioner keeps a main office in Cedartown and a second one in Rockmart, so sellers in both towns have a counter close to home.

The county's population grew from 42,853 at the 2020 census, and it packs 138.1 people into each of its 310.34 square miles of land. Renters are common here: only 66.0% of homes are owner-occupied, the lowest rate among these counties. About 15.1% of residents identify as Hispanic or Latino, and 12.1% speak a language other than English at home.

That mix shapes who buys. A larger rental share means a seller may be a landlord, and a house with tenants in place needs its own plan for showings and closing.

sections.h2: How affordable is housing in Polk County?
sections.html:
Polk is the least expensive of the group. The 2020-2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $187,600, and median household income is $58,515.

sections.h2: Which Polk County office does what?
sections.html:
The assessors value your property and the tax commissioner bills it. Polk is unusual because the tax commissioner keeps two offices.

  • Main tax office: 144 West Ave, Cedartown, GA 30125.
  • Rockmart tax office: 316 N Piedmont Ave, Rockmart, GA 30153.
  • Phone and email: (770) 749-2125 and taxoffice@polkga.org. Both offices run 9 am to 5 pm on weekdays and close for lunch from 12:45 to 2:00 pm.
  • Board of Assessors: (770) 749-2108. It values property, receives returns and approves exemptions.
  • Board of Equalization: appointed by the Grand Jury to hear value appeals.

The county does not collect city tax. Each city within Polk bills and collects its own, so a house inside Cedartown or Rockmart can carry a second bill. Ask the city clerk for that payoff separately.

sections.h2: When is the Polk County property tax bill due?
sections.html:
Read the due date printed on your bill. The tax commissioner's FAQ says real estate and business personal property are normally due December 20, while the county's own tax commissioner page says taxes are due sixty days from the date bills were mailed.

The FAQ describes the cost of paying late in three parts. Interest of 1% per month starts after the due date. A 10% penalty applies to anything unpaid after 90 days, but homesteaded property with a liability under $500 is spared that penalty. After 90 days the account is also open to a FIFA recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, and the FAQ points out that credit bureaus can read these public records.

Bills go to the owner, never to a mortgage company, so an escrow customer has to forward the bill. Mobile and manufactured homes follow separate dates, which the tax commissioner's site lists, so check that site before relying on the real estate deadline.

sections.h2: How are Polk County values set and challenged?
sections.html:
Every property is valued as of January 1, and the assessed amount is 40% of that fair market value. The county board of assessors mailed its 2026 assessment notices on July 17, 2026, and the appeal window runs 45 days from the date of a notice.

To appeal, write to the Polk County Board of Tax Assessors, which decides whether to change the value. A taxpayer can take the case to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator and later to Superior Court by filing written notice. The grounds can be value, uniformity or taxability.

The assessor's page also offers a tax estimator on qpublic.net/ga/polk. Pick the correct tax district, enter the market value from your notice, then subtract the estimated tax savings shown on the notice. The county calls the result only an estimate, since final millage rates can change it.

sections.h2: What exemptions apply to Polk County homes?
sections.html:
To receive a homestead exemption you must have owned the property on January 1, use it as your legal residence, and not claim a homestead anywhere else. Applications can be made at any time of year but must arrive by April 1 for that year's bill.

  • The basic exemption covers the first $2,000 of assessed value on county, state and school tax.
  • Owners aged 65 or older may claim $20,000 off school tax and $4,000 off county tax.
  • Owners aged 62 may qualify for extra relief when income for owner and spouse is under $10,000.
  • Owners aged 70 may qualify for extra relief when household income is under $10,000.
  • Veterans who are 100% permanently disabled qualify for an added exemption.

Only one home can be homesteaded at a time. When you move, you apply again for the new address.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Polk County house when taxes are unpaid?
sections.html:
Get a written payoff first, then clear it from the sale proceeds. Polk's tax commissioner says it does not sell tax liens, but a FIFA can still be recorded against the property after 90 days.

  1. Call (770) 749-2125 and ask for the balance with interest and penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA is on file with the Clerk of Superior Court.
  3. If the house is inside a city, request the city's balance too.
  4. Ask the closing attorney to list each payoff on the settlement statement.

Selling before penalties stack up keeps more of your equity. If repairs, tenants or an inherited title are slowing a regular listing, a cash buyer who buys as-is can set a closing date and pay the tax from the proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Polk County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Check the date on your bill. The tax commissioner's FAQ lists December 20 for real estate, and the county page says bills are due sixty days after mailing.

faqs.q: What penalty does Polk County charge for late taxes?
faqs.a: Interest of 1% per month begins after the due date, and a 10% penalty applies to taxes unpaid after 90 days. Homesteaded property with less than $500 owed is exempt from that penalty.

faqs.q: Where is the Polk County tax office?
faqs.a: The main office is at 144 West Ave in Cedartown, and a second office is at 316 N Piedmont Ave in Rockmart. The phone number is (770) 749-2125.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Polk County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. For 2026, the notices went out July 17, so that window has already closed.

faqs.q: Does Polk County collect city property tax?
faqs.a: No. The county's tax commissioner page says cities in the county bill and collect their own tax, so contact the city clerk for a city payoff.
